notes: PC build of AdTrapper v11.15: THE OWNER'S SHIELD (owner orders 2026-11-04). Two changes on top of 11.14; everything else -- pastel Settings and front, verdict pills, boom text, threat feed, disclaimer v3.1 -- is identical to 11.14. (1) Temu (com.einnovation.temu) joins the built-in shield by exact package name, in the Carrier Shield family: the field scan flagged it REVIEW off the shop's learned-removed rule while its Background Check came back CLEARED, and the owner ruled it protected. (2) A new fifth door on a flagged app's card, SHIELD THIS APP, in the same strip as Add to remove list / Keep item / Background check / UN-LEARN: one tap puts that app on the owner's own shield -- a persistent user_shield.json beside the program, outside the program file, so it survives every future flip -- and from then on the app stands exactly where a Carrier Shield app stands in scan and Background Check, never flagged by the learned rule, the keyword classes, the census or ad software. The card reflects the shield at once (clean, no longer counted as flagged), the row wears an ON THE SHOP SHIELD line, and the Activity log records it. HARD LIMIT, the standing law: a shield never overrides a conviction -- an app on the KNOWN_BAD bad list cannot be shielded; the door refuses it in plain words. CUSTOMER LOCKOUT: the door is live only on the shop build -- the new BUILD_CHANNEL constant ("shop" in this shelf build) gates it; a customer build renders the same door grayed out and its handler a no-op. Twin of the Mac 11.15 build; ANDROID PARITY STILL OWED before any flip (Temu in the phone guard, the phone's own Shield door with the same Play lockout) -- paired-release law.
